title: Retinal-image models detect diabetic kidney disease across multiple cohorts
summary: A retinal-image model trained for diabetic kidney disease achieved AUCs of 0.791–0.826 across ten external datasets totaling 65,406 participants. A separate task distinguished isolated diabetic nephropathy from other kidney disease in small biopsy-referenced cohorts. These results support diagnostic investigation without establishing improved patient outcomes or replacement of confirmatory tests.
organization: Shanghai Sixth People’s Hospital; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

source_review.scope: Version-specific original computational/statistical Methods and Results plus primary bibliographic dates. Clinical benefit, causal effects and independent replication are not inferred.

evidence.tested: DeepDKD used 734,084 pretraining images and 486,312 development/internal-validation images from 121,578 participants. The image-only classifier averaged scores across each participant’s available images. Internal DKD AUC was .842; ten external cohorts had AUC .791–.826. The biopsy-related task used 267 development participants and 244 external participants, with external AUC .733–.844. A 325-person prospective primary-care proof-of-concept reported sensitivity 89.8% and specificity 47.6% against subsequent confirmatory findings.
evidence.unknown: The represented principal result is retrospective multicohort diagnostic validation. External datasets and a prospectively collected cohort do not establish improved clinical outcomes. Camera/domain differences and population selection constrain transfer. The small prospective study selected a previously defined high-sensitivity operating point; specificity was low, and the apparent specificity improvement versus metadata was not significant (P=.072). Model-development split details and diagnostic-reference definitions are in an appendix not independently read here. The retinal model is an ancillary screen, not a non-invasive tissue biopsy or proven substitute for laboratory/biopsy confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: Contrastively pretrained image features were supervised for kidney-disease categories; a frozen image encoder and linear classifier supported the separate nephropathy task.
